skill.name: cookoff
skill.description: Orchestrates a design-to-implementation workflow that can compare parallel agent implementations from one shared design and select a winner.
skill.summary: Compare parallel implementations from one design before choosing a final path.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backticks, fenced examples, or inline skill names rather than Ruby shell execution. The only confirmed risk is the cleanup block that instructs deletion of git worktrees and branches, which can remove local work if used incorrectly. No evidence found of prompt injection or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running git worktree remove or git branch -D, and show exact targets first.
State that placeholders must be validated and commands should run only inside the intended repository.

static_findings.snippet: - `cookoff` - Same design, multiple cooks compete (each creates own plan + implements)
| `writing-plans` | `superpowers:writing-plans` | Each agent writes their own implementation plan |
| `executing-plans` | `superpowers:executing-plans` | Execute plan tasks sequentially with verificat
| `parallel-agents` | `superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents` | Dispatch multiple Task tools in si
| `verification` | `superpowers:verification-before-completion` | Run command, read output, THEN cla
| `fresh-eyes` | `fresh-eyes-review:skills` (2389) | 2-5 min review for security, logic, edge cases
| `judge` | `test-kitchen:judge` | Scoring framework with checklists (MUST invoke at Phase 4) |
Use `parallel-agents` pattern. Send ONE message with multiple Task tool calls:
| `writing-plans` | 3 | Each subagent creates their own implementation plan |
| `parallel-agents` | 3 | Dispatch ALL subagents in SINGLE message |
| `verification` | 3, 5 | Before claiming done; before declaring winner |
| `judge` | 4 | **INVOKE** for scoring framework (loads fresh, ensures format compliance) |
Reason: Clean fresh-eyes review, solid data-layer-first architecture

content.value_statement: Choosing one implementation path can miss better designs. This skill runs parallel agent implementations from the same design, then compares results before cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Offers implementation choices when a design is ready.
Assesses feature complexity and recommends an implementation count.
Defines a directory structure for plans and cookoff results.
Guides parallel agent dispatch from one shared design document.
Compares implementations using tests, review findings, and scoring.
Records the selected winner and cleanup decisions.
limitations: Requires an existing design or a clear implementation agreement.
Depends on separate planning, execution, review, and judge skills when available.
Uses git worktrees and shell commands that need repository context.
Cannot guarantee independent solutions if agents reuse the same assumptions.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Feature Builds
use_cases.description: Run several independent implementations of one approved feature design before selecting the strongest result.

use_cases.title: Reduce Implementation Risk
use_cases.description: Compare test results, review findings, and design adherence before accepting a higher risk code change.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent Work
use_cases.description: Use separate agents to plan and implement in parallel while keeping outputs organized for review.

prompt_templates.title: Start Implementation Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for moving from an approved design to implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have approved this design. Use cookoff to help me choose the implementation approach.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Complexity
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for deciding how many implementations to run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read docs/plans/<feature>/design.md and recommend how many parallel implementations we should run. Explain the risk signals.

prompt_templates.title: Run Parallel Cookoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for coordinating independent implementation agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a cookoff with three independent implementation agents. Each agent should write its own plan from the shared design, implement it, run tests, and report results.

prompt_templates.title: Judge and Finish
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for comparing completed implementations and closing the workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the completed implementations using test results, review findings, design adherence, and maintainability. Recommend a winner and identify cleanup steps that need my confirmation.

output_examples.input: User says: Let us build the approved authentication design.
output_examples.output: The skill offers single agent, cookoff, or local implementation. It recommends three implementations because authentication adds medium risk.

output_examples.input: User selects a three-agent cookoff for a medium feature.
output: Each agent receives the same design and writes an independent plan.
Each implementation runs tests and reports changed files and issues.
Results are compared before a winner is recommended.

output_examples.input: All implementation teams have reported test and review results.
output_examples.output: The skill compares design adherence, tests, review findings, and maintainability. It records the winner and lists cleanup steps for confirmation.

best_practices: Start from a design document with stable requirements.
Ask every agent to create an independent plan before implementation.
Confirm cleanup commands before deleting worktrees or branches.
anti_patterns: Starting a cookoff from vague requirements.
Sharing one detailed implementation plan across all agents.
Deleting losing worktrees before the winner has been verified.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an implementation cookoff where multiple agents build from the same design and compare results.

faq.question: Does it write code itself?
faq.answer: It guides the workflow. Code is produced by selected agents or the local session.

faq.question: How many implementations should I run?
faq.answer: The skill maps feature complexity to an implementation count, usually two to five.

faq.question: Does it require git worktrees?
faq.answer: It is designed around git worktrees, but teams can adapt the workflow to another isolation method.

faq.question: How is the winner chosen?
faq.answer: The workflow compares tests, design adherence, fresh review findings, and scoring from a judge step.

faq.question: Is cleanup automatic?
faq.answer: No. Treat cleanup as a confirmation step, especially when deleting branches or worktrees.
